collection_summary:
Original `factual_lookup` instance that **SATURATES the 5th fully-cleared category** at 5/5 (factual_lookup goes from gap 1 to gap 0, joining multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5). **Technology/Civil Engineering subdomain** — second instance under Civil Engineering, joining `notable_bridges_by_main_span` (Technology family extends from 3 to 4 instances with this Ready; Civil Engineering subdomain 1 → 2). Natural human query: 'What are the world's tallest dams — how tall is each, what country are they in, what river, and when was each completed?'

Multi-wiki source plan (21 URLs): 1 Wikipedia 'List of tallest dams' master article supplies the universe + ranking (top-20 by structural height, man-made only); 20 per-dam Wikipedia articles supply per-row Height + Country + River + Year Completed via lead/infobox sections.

Result: 20 rows × 5 columns (Dam PK + Height (m) numeric + Country categorical + River categorical + Year Completed numeric), single-key PK on Dam, 0 duplicates. Country distribution: China 7 (dominates modern dam-engineering — Jinping-I, Lianghekou, Xiaowan, Baihetan, Xiluodu, Nuozhadu, Laxiwa), Switzerland 2 (Grande Dixence + Mauvoisin alpine arch legacy), Turkey 2 (Yusufeli + Deriner Çoruh cascade), plus singletons for Tajikistan, Georgia, Italy, Mexico, India, Ethiopia, Colombia, Canada, Russia (12 distinct countries). Height range: 242-305 m (63 m span). Year Completed range: 1957 (Mauvoisin) to 2022 (Yusufeli) — 65 years of major-dam engineering.

Universe rule: top-20 completed man-made dams by structural height per Wikipedia 'List of tallest dams' master article's 'Existing' section ranking. Natural-origin entries in the master table (Usoi 567 m landslide dam, The Barrier 500 m lava dam, Lake Waikaremoana 250 m landslide dam) are EXCLUDED because the master article's lead explicitly foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam' (distinguishing built dams from natural-formation dams), and the Year Completed schema column does not semantically apply to natural formation events (BCE dates, geological events). This man-made-only scoping mirrors the `notable_bridges_by_main_span` instance's engineered-structures-only universe.

Entity class: `engineered-structures/dams` (NEW fine-class in the under-represented `engineered-structures` bucket — bucket extends from 2 to 3 instances after this Ready, joining bridges and buildings).

Bridges-cycle lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Dam using Wikipedia common-form names with disambiguators preserved per article title (Gilgel Gibe III, Jinping-I with hyphen-Roman-numeral, Chicoasén with acute é, Sayano-Shushenskaya with hyphen); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (master + per-dam), 21 URLs total; (c) explicit man-made-only universe rule documented in temporal_note + decision_log; (d) `source_defined` claim type honestly reflects the top-20-by-master-ranking universe; (e) canonical-source rule from cycle-2 bridges applied with cycle-2-of-this-instance refinement: 2 Height exceptions (Gilgel Gibe III 250 m per per-dam-wins clause vs master 243 m; Mica Dam 243 m per master-fallback clause because per-dam article internally inconsistent at infobox 240 vs body 244) + 4 Year Completed discrepancies (per-dam article lead wins over master-table 'Completed' column when they disagree). Cycle-2 of this instance added the master-fallback clause to handle per-dam internal inconsistency.
source_coverage_notes:
Twenty-one Wikipedia source URLs combine. One 'List of tallest dams' master article defines the universe + ranking (the master article maintains a single ranked table by structural height); 20 per-dam articles supply per-row attribute values via infobox / lead sections.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_dams): universe + ranking. Article lead defines scope as 'tallest dams in the world above 150 m' and foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam in the world at 305 m'. Master table columns: Name | Height | Type | Country | River | Completed. The Type column flags 3 natural-origin entries (Usoi 'Landslide', The Barrier 'Lava', Lake Waikaremoana 'Landslide') which are EXCLUDED from the staged universe per the man-made-only rule. Master ranking is by structural height (foundation to crest) — the article does not distinguish hydraulic head from structural height. Master article has 'Existing' + 'Under construction' sections; staged entries are all from 'Existing'.

Per-dam Wikipedia articles (per-row attribute grounding):
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinping-I_Dam): Height = 305 m (infobox + lead concur); Country = China; River = Yalong River; Year Completed = 2014 (per-dam article lead 'completed in 2014, first power 2013'). Cycle-1 staging: Year 2014 follows per-dam article lead (master-table reports 2013 which is the first-power year; per-dam canonical-source-rule wins for Year Completed because per-dam article lead + infobox concur on 2014 as the completion year).
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurek_Dam): 300 m; Tajikistan; Vakhsh River; 1980.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lianghekou_Dam): 295 m; China; Yalong River; 2021.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaowan_Dam): 292 m; China; Lancang River (upper Mekong); 2010.
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baihetan_Dam): 289 m; China; Jinsha River; Year Completed = 2021 (opening ceremony Feb 2021 per per-dam article lead; full operation reached Dec 2022 per article body — staged value 2021 follows the article-lead opening-ceremony framing).
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiluodu_Dam): 285.5 m; China; Jinsha River; 2013.
- source_urls[7] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grande_Dixence_Dam): 285 m; Switzerland; Dixence; Year Completed = 1961 (article lead 'construction completed in 1961, fully commissioned in 1965'; master-table reports 1964 — staged value 1961 follows the per-dam canonical-source-rule for completion year vs commissioning year).
- source_urls[8] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enguri_Dam): 271.5 m; Georgia; Enguri River; 1978 (temporarily operational 1978 per per-dam article; fully completed 1987; staged 1978 matches the article-lead operational-completion framing and the master table).
- source_urls[9] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yusufeli_Dam): 270 m; Turkey; Çoruh River; Year Completed = 2022 (per-dam article lead 'operational at end of 2022, reservoir began filling April 2023'; master-table reports 2021 — staged 2022 follows per-dam canonical-source rule).
- source_urls[10] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vajont_Dam): 262 m; Italy; Vajont (river); Year Completed = 1959 (structurally completed 1959; dam is 'Disused' post-1963 disaster but structural completion is the staged value, mirroring how the schema column is 'Year Completed' not 'Year Operational'). Master-table reports 261.6 m height; per-dam article 262 m — minor rounding difference, staged 262 m per per-dam canonical-source rule.
- source_urls[11] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuozhadu_Dam): 261.5 m; China; Lancang River; 2012.
- source_urls[12] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicoas%C3%A9n_Dam): 261 m; Mexico; Grijalva River; 1980. Note: Wikipedia article title is 'Chicoasén Dam' (Spanish acute é per article); official Spanish name 'Presa Manuel Moreno Torres' is a redirect. Staged Wikipedia common-form 'Chicoasén Dam' with é preserved per article title.
- source_urls[13] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehri_Dam): 260.5 m; India; Bhagirathi River; 2006.
- source_urls[14] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilgel_Gibe_III_Dam): Height = 250 m (per-dam article infobox + lead both report 250 m); Ethiopia; Omo River; Year Completed = 2015. **Cycle-1 source discrepancy** (Pingnan-Third-style): master-table reports 243 m for Gilgel Gibe III; per-dam article infobox + lead concur on 250 m. Per the cycle-2 bridges-instance canonical-source rule (per-dam article wins for Height value when per-dam infobox + lead concur and master-table value is unsupported by per-dam sourcing), staged value is 250 m. This means the staged height-sorted order (Gilgel Gibe III at 250 m alongside Mauvoisin and Laxiwa) differs from the master-table rank position (which had Gilgel Gibe III at rank 19 based on 243 m). The universe set is unchanged (same 20 dams whether sorted by master rank or by per-dam canonical values).
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxiwa_Dam): 250 m; China; Yellow River; 2009.
- source_urls[16] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauvoisin_Dam): 250 m; Switzerland; Dranse de Bagnes; 1957.
- source_urls[17] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deriner_Dam): 249 m; Turkey; Çoruh River; 2012.
- source_urls[18] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Lleras_Dam): 243 m; Colombia; Guavio River; 1989. Note: 'Guavio Dam' is a redirect; staged Wikipedia common-form 'Alberto Lleras Dam' per article title.
- source_urls[19] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mica_Dam): Height = 243 m (master-table value, staged per master-fallback rule); Canada; Columbia River; 1973. **Cycle-2 source discrepancy** (master-fallback exception, distinct from the Gilgel Gibe III per-dam-wins exception): per-dam article is internally INCONSISTENT — infobox reports 240 m while body text reports 244 m. The cycle-2-refined canonical-source rule says per-dam article wins for Height ONLY when per-dam infobox + lead/body concur; when per-dam article is internally inconsistent, the master-table value is the canonical fallback (because no single per-dam value is internally supported). Staged 243 m per master. Note that 243 m is the median between the per-dam infobox 240 and body 244, but the staged choice is master-fallback rule, not arithmetic-median (which would coincidentally give 242 m).
- source_urls[20] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayano-Shushenskaya_Dam): 242 m; Russia; Yenisei River; 1985. Hyphen preserved per Wikipedia article title.

Validation note: every (Dam, Height, Country, River, Year Completed) tuple is grounded in (a) the master 'List of tallest dams' article confirming the dam's place in the top-20 man-made ranking, and (b) the per-dam Wikipedia article supplying per-row attribute values via lead/infobox. Height values match between master and per-dam article for 18 of 20 rows; two exceptions: (i) Gilgel Gibe III Dam (250 m per-dam vs 243 m master) — resolved by adopting the per-dam value per the per-dam-wins canonical-source rule because per-dam infobox + lead concur on 250 m and master is unsupported; (ii) Mica Dam (243 m master vs per-dam infobox 240 m + per-dam body 244 m — internally inconsistent) — resolved by adopting the master-table value 243 m per the cycle-2-refined master-fallback rule because per-dam article does not provide a single internally-consistent value. Year Completed values differ between master and per-dam article for 4 rows (Jinping-I 2014/2013, Yusufeli 2022/2021, Grande Dixence 1961/1964, Baihetan 2021 article-lead opening-ceremony framing) — all resolved in favor of per-dam article lead per the canonical-source rule.

**Canonical-source rule (refined in cycle 2 of this instance, building on cycle-2 bridges Pingnan-Third precedent):**
- Per-dam article wins for Height/Year Completed when per-dam infobox + lead/body concur on a value AND the master-table value is unsupported by per-dam sourcing. Examples: Gilgel Gibe III (250 m per-dam concur > master 243 m); Jinping-I 2014 (per-dam concur > master 2013).
- Master-table wins for Height/Year Completed when per-dam article is internally inconsistent (infobox vs lead vs body disagree on the value) — master-table is the canonical fallback because no single per-dam value is internally supported. Example: Mica Dam 243 m (master, with per-dam infobox 240 m + per-dam body 244 m internally inconsistent).
- Master per-list ranking wins for the universe-membership rule (which 20 dams qualify), regardless of which Height value is used in the row.

Universe-size sanity: 20 staged rows = top-20 man-made completed dams per Wikipedia master article 'Existing' section ranking, with 3 natural-origin entries excluded (Usoi, The Barrier, Lake Waikaremoana — all flagged in master table's Type column as Landslide/Lava). The master article enumerates ~50+ dams in its full 'Existing' section ranging down to ~150 m floor; the staged 20 are the top-K-by-height subset under the man-made-only filter.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md 4-axis rubric):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks resolved at staging. R1: master article's lead foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam' but master table's top-2 entries (Usoi 567 m, The Barrier 500 m) are natural landslide/lava dams — committed to man-made-only universe rule at Stage-1 (mirrors bridges-instance engineered-structures-only scope; the Year Completed schema column does not semantically apply to natural formation events). R2: master-table vs per-dam article Height discrepancy on Gilgel Gibe III (243 m master vs 250 m per-dam) — committed to per-dam canonical-source-rule at Stage-1 (carrying forward the cycle-2 bridges Pingnan-Third precedent). R3: master-table vs per-dam article Year Completed discrepancies on 4 rows (Jinping-I, Yusufeli, Grande Dixence, Baihetan) — committed to per-dam article-lead-foregrounded year per the canonical-source rule.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses tallest dams. Closest seed-in-shape is the longest-rivers (top-K by physical dimension) and tallest-buildings (engineered-structures top-K) seeds — dams are a same-shape entity class in an under-represented bucket.
- Category: factual_lookup (primary — single-cell-per-row attribute lookup over a fixed top-20 entity set; saturates 5th category at 5/5). Secondary: top_k (universe rule is top-K by structural height). The factual_lookup framing is justified by the schema shape (each row is one dam with 4 source-grounded attribute lookups); the top_k secondary classification reflects the universe-membership rule.
- Source plan: 21 Wikipedia URLs (1 master + 20 per-dam). Master defines universe + ranking; per-dam articles supply per-row attribute values.
- Expected shape: 20 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Dam.
- Domain: Technology/Civil Engineering — extends the same domain family as `notable_bridges_by_main_span` (Civil Engineering subdomain becomes 2 instances). Domain novelty: Neutral (subdomain exists but light).
- Entity-class diversity: `engineered-structures/dams` NEW fine-class. Bucket `engineered-structures/*` extends from 2 to 3 instances (joining bridges + buildings). Entity-class novelty: Good (NEW fine-class in under-represented bucket).
- 4-axis rubric scoring: Seed source Bad (Original) + Category gap Good (gap-1 saturates 5th category) + Domain novelty Neutral (subdomain light) + Entity novelty Good (NEW fine-class in under-rep bucket) = ★★★ overall.
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) row count 20 is at the upper end of the standard 15-25 band; (b) China dominates the top-20 ranking (7 of 20 = 35%) — same modern-engineering pattern as bridges; (c) Vajont Dam staged despite 'Disused' operational status — flagged in source_coverage_notes as structural completion ≠ operational status; (d) Height discrepancies on 2 of 20 rows (Gilgel Gibe III per-dam-wins; Mica master-fallback) — within Pingnan-Third precedent comfort zone, both documented with explicit canonical-source rule clauses.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe rule: top-20 completed man-made dams by structural height per Wikipedia 'List of tallest dams' master article 'Existing' section ranking. Natural-origin entries excluded (3 rows: Usoi 567 m landslide dam Tajikistan; The Barrier 500 m lava dam Canada; Lake Waikaremoana 250 m landslide dam New Zealand). Justification: (a) master article's lead foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam', acknowledging the natural/man-made distinction; (b) master table's Type column explicitly flags natural-origin entries; (c) Year Completed schema column does not semantically apply to natural formation events (geological-era dates would break the numeric-integer-year convention); (d) the bridges-instance engineered-structures-only scoping precedent applies analogously.
2) Height canonical-source rule (cycle-2 refined, building on cycle-2 bridges Pingnan-Third precedent): two-clause rule. Clause A (per-dam-wins): per-dam article wins for Height when per-dam infobox + lead/body concur and master-table value is unsupported by per-dam sourcing. Applied to 1 row: Gilgel Gibe III Dam — staged 250 m per per-dam article (per-dam infobox + lead both report 250 m; master-table 243 m is unsupported). Clause B (master-fallback): master-table wins for Height when per-dam article is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT (infobox vs lead vs body disagree on the value), because no single per-dam value is internally supported. Applied to 1 row: Mica Dam — staged 243 m per master-table (per-dam infobox 240 m vs per-dam body 244 m — internally inconsistent; master 243 m is the canonical fallback). Cycle-2 audit (cycle 1 of this instance) caught the Mica case as a BLOCKING factual finding because the cycle-1 narrative claimed 'Height values match between master and per-dam article for 19 of 20 rows' — which was wrong: 18 of 20 match cleanly, plus the Gilgel Gibe III per-dam-wins exception and the Mica master-fallback exception. The cycle-2 refinement extends the canonical-source rule to handle per-dam internal inconsistency. Universe set is unchanged.
3) Year Completed canonical-source rule (per-dam article lead wins over master-table cell): applied to 4 rows. Jinping-I 2014 (per-dam article 'completed 2014, first power 2013'; master 2013 is first-power year). Yusufeli 2022 (per-dam article 'operational end of 2022'; master 2021 is too early). Grande Dixence 1961 (per-dam article 'construction completed 1961, commissioned 1965'; master 1964 is between these). Baihetan 2021 (per-dam article 'opening ceremony Feb 2021, full operation Dec 2022'; master 2021 — concurs, staged 2021 per opening-ceremony framing).
4) Dam name normalization: Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved per article title. Special-character handling: 'Chicoasén Dam' uses Spanish acute é (U+00E9) per article title; 'Jinping-I Dam' uses hyphen-Roman-numeral per article; 'Sayano-Shushenskaya Dam' uses hyphen per article; 'Gilgel Gibe III Dam' keeps the III qualifier (distinguishes from Gilgel Gibe I + II + IV cascade members on the same Omo system). 'Alberto Lleras Dam' preferred over 'Guavio Dam' redirect (article title is the Wikipedia canonical name).
5) Height (m) values: numeric metres per per-dam article infobox + master-table column (concurring values for 18 of 20 rows; Gilgel Gibe III per-dam-wins exception + Mica master-fallback exception per Decision 2). Two-decimal precision (X.5 m) is used for 4 rows (Xiluodu 285.5, Enguri 271.5, Nuozhadu 261.5, Tehri 260.5) per per-dam article values; remaining 16 rows are integer metres. Vajont 262 m (per-dam) vs 261.6 m (master) resolved at 262 m per per-dam canonical-source rule (both per-dam infobox and lead concur at 262).
6) Country values: 12 distinct countries (China 7, Switzerland 2, Turkey 2, plus 9 singletons for Tajikistan, Georgia, Italy, Mexico, India, Ethiopia, Colombia, Canada, Russia). All staged values are sovereign-state-level per per-dam article infobox 'Country' field. No sub-national qualifiers needed.
7) River values: 17 distinct rivers (Yalong River, Vakhsh River, Lancang River 2, Jinsha River 2, Dixence, Enguri River, Çoruh River 2, Vajont, Grijalva River, Bhagirathi River, Omo River, Yellow River, Dranse de Bagnes, Guavio River, Columbia River, Yenisei River). Per-dam article infobox 'River' field is the primary river dammed; for cascade systems (Lancang River = upper Mekong; Jinsha River = upper Yangtze), staged value matches per-dam article's primary naming.
8) Year Completed: numeric integer per per-dam article-lead 'completed' / 'opened' / 'first impoundment' year. For dams with multi-year construction phases or staged commissioning (Grande Dixence, Enguri, Vajont, Baihetan), staged year is the per-dam article-lead foregrounded completion year per Decision 3.
9) Sort order: Height (m) DESC primary (tallest-first), Dam ASC alphabetical secondary tiebreaker. For Height=250 three-way tie (Gilgel Gibe III, Laxiwa, Mauvoisin): alphabetical ordering G < L < M. For Height=243 two-way tie (Alberto Lleras, Mica): alphabetical A < M.
10) operation_type 'filter' chosen — top-K-by-height + structural-height + man-made + completed is a multi-predicate filter operation. 'aggregation' was considered (GROUP BY country) but rejected because the universe is the top-20 directly, not a per-country aggregate.
11) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is master-article-defined top-20 with the man-made-only filter rule. NOT `exhaustive` because the master article enumerates ~50+ dams down to a 150 m floor (only top-20 staged). NOT `partially_supplemented` because every row + every attribute is fully source-grounded across master + per-dam URLs.
normalization_decisions: Dam (PK) values use Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved per article title. Special-character handling: 'Chicoasén Dam' uses Spanish acute é (U+00E9) per Wikipedia title; 'Jinping-I Dam' uses ASCII hyphen + Roman numeral I per article title; 'Sayano-Shushenskaya Dam' uses ASCII hyphen per article title; 'Gilgel Gibe III Dam' uses ASCII space + Roman numeral III per article title (distinguishes from cascade siblings Gilgel Gibe I, II, IV). Redirect targets: 'Guavio Dam' redirects to 'Alberto Lleras Dam'; staged form is the article title 'Alberto Lleras Dam'. Height (m) is numeric metres per per-dam article infobox 'Height' field; values match master-table for 18 of 20 rows. Two Height exceptions per the cycle-2-refined canonical-source rule: Gilgel Gibe III Dam uses 250 m per per-dam infobox + lead concur, deviating from master-table 243 m (per-dam-wins clause); Mica Dam uses 243 m per master-table because per-dam article is internally inconsistent (infobox 240 m vs body 244 m, master-fallback clause). Four rows use 0.5 m precision (Xiluodu 285.5, Enguri 271.5, Nuozhadu 261.5, Tehri 260.5) per per-dam article values; remaining 16 rows are integer metres. Country is a single categorical value per per-dam article infobox 'Country' field (12 distinct values across staged rows). River is a single categorical value per per-dam article infobox 'River' field (17 distinct values, with shared rivers for cascade dams on same waterway: Yalong River 2, Lancang River 2, Jinsha River 2, Çoruh River 2). Year Completed is numeric integer per per-dam article-lead 'completed' / 'opened' / 'first impoundment' year (master-table 'Completed' column overruled for 4 rows per per-dam canonical-source rule). Sort: Height (m) DESC primary, Dam ASC secondary tiebreaker.
open_questions: 1) Man-made vs natural-origin universe rule: 3 natural-origin entries (Usoi 567 m landslide dam Tajikistan 1911-formed; The Barrier 500 m lava dam Canada ~11,000 BCE; Lake Waikaremoana 250 m landslide dam New Zealand ~200 BCE) are excluded from the staged universe per the man-made-only rule (mirrors bridges-instance engineered-only scope). An audit could challenge this by proposing a broader universe (top-20 dams including natural-origin) — that would require either reframing Year Completed to handle BCE dates or splitting the schema. Cycle-1 staged the cleaner man-made-only rule. 2) Gilgel Gibe III Dam Height discrepancy: staged 250 m per per-dam canonical-source rule; master-table reports 243 m. An LLM answering 243 m would be responding to the master-list cell rather than the more-detailed per-dam article. Both readings are source-defensible; staged value follows the cycle-2-refined canonical-source rule. 3) Year Completed for dams with staged commissioning (Grande Dixence, Enguri, Vajont, Baihetan): staged value is the per-dam article-lead foregrounded completion year. For Grande Dixence (1961 vs 1965 commissioned), Enguri (1978 partial vs 1987 full), and Yusufeli (2022 operational vs 2023 reservoir-filled), an LLM answering the alternative commissioning/operational year would be responding to a different milestone in the dam's lifecycle. 4) Vajont Dam staged despite 'Disused' operational status post-1963 disaster: dam was structurally completed 1959 (master + per-dam article concur); the disaster did not destroy the dam structure (the landslide overtopped it without breaching). 'Disused' is operational status, not completion status — the staged Year Completed 1959 is defensible per the schema column's semantics. An LLM answering with the disaster year 1963 or with 'never operational' would be responding to the lifecycle context rather than the completion year. 5) Country grouping for Hong Kong-style sub-national cases: all 20 staged China entries are mainland China (no Hong Kong / Taiwan / Macau dams in the top-20), so the bridges-instance master-list-grouping-over-sub-national rule does not need to apply here. 6) Cascade-river naming: Yalong River 2 dams (Jinping-I, Lianghekou), Lancang River 2 dams (Xiaowan, Nuozhadu), Jinsha River 2 dams (Baihetan, Xiluodu), Çoruh River 2 dams (Yusufeli, Deriner). For each cascade pair, per-dam articles use the same river-name convention (no sub-tributary qualifier needed). An LLM answering 'Mekong River' for Lancang River would be responding to the downstream-international name (Mekong is the post-China name for Lancang downstream of Jinghong); staged value Lancang River matches the per-dam article. 7) Xiluodu Dam height 285.5 m vs Grande Dixence 285 m: very close ranks (Xiluodu #6, Grande Dixence #7). The 0.5 m difference is from per-dam article precision (Xiluodu reports 285.5 m per article infobox; Grande Dixence reports 285 m as rounded integer per article). An LLM answering Xiluodu 285 m or Grande Dixence 285.5 m would be a minor precision-rounding error. 8) Mauvoisin Dam height 250 m: per-dam article reports 250 m (integer). Wikipedia History section notes that an earlier 237 m structure was raised by 13 m in 1991 to the current 250 m. Staged Year Completed 1957 follows the original-completion-year framing (the 1991 raise is documented but not the primary completion event). An LLM answering 1991 would be responding to the height-raise milestone; staged 1957 is the structural-completion year per per-dam article lead. 9) Hydraulic head vs structural height: master article ranks by structural height (foundation to crest); no per-dam article in the staged 20 advertises a hydraulic-head ranking that would conflict. An LLM answering with hydraulic head values (e.g., Grande Dixence has very high effective head through penstocks to underground turbines) would be responding to a different engineering metric than structural height. Staged column is structural height per master article convention. 10) Disambiguation case: 'Gilgel Gibe III Dam' could be confused with sibling cascade dams Gilgel Gibe I, II, IV on the Omo system. Staged form preserves the III qualifier to distinguish.
proposed_supplements:
The 20-row staged universe is a curator-bounded subset of the world's tallest dams per the Wikipedia master article. Two curator-decided scope choices are documented:

(1) Top-K cutoff choice (20 vs 15 vs 25): the staged top-20 is the row-count sweet spot (within standard 15-25 band, gives enough variety for non-key attribute calibration, captures the visible-engineering-threshold ~242 m floor). Alternatives:
- Top-15 (15 rows): would lose the bottom-5 entries (Mauvoisin, Deriner, Alberto Lleras, Mica, Sayano-Shushenskaya). Plausible alternative but loses the 1957 Mauvoisin (alpine arch dam history) and the 1985 Sayano-Shushenskaya (Soviet hydroelectric legacy).
- Top-25 (25 rows): would add Ertan Dam 240 m China 1999 + Changheba Dam 240 m China 2017 + 3 more sub-240 m entries. Plausible but adds row-count complexity beyond the 15-25 band sweet spot.
- Top-20 (staged): captures the 242-305 m height range with 63 m span; includes all 'visible-engineering-threshold' dams above 240 m.

(2) Man-made-only vs all-dams universe rule: staged man-made-only excludes 3 natural-origin entries (Usoi, The Barrier, Lake Waikaremoana). Alternative all-dams universe would include these 3, giving:
- Usoi Dam 567 m Tajikistan 1911 (landslide-formed during Pamir earthquake)
- The Barrier 500 m Canada ~11,000 BCE (lava dam from volcanic eruption)
- Lake Waikaremoana 250 m New Zealand ~200 BCE (landslide-formed)
This would shift the universe to top-20-of-all-tall-dams (different curator-judgment on natural vs man-made). Rejected because (a) the schema's Year Completed column does not semantically apply to geological-era formation events; (b) the master article's lead explicitly foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam' (acknowledging the distinction); (c) the bridges-instance engineered-structures-only scoping precedent applies analogously.

(3) Hydraulic-head vs structural-height ranking: staged structural-height per master article convention. Alternative hydraulic-head ranking would re-rank multiple dams (Grande Dixence's effective head through penstocks is significantly more than its 285 m structural height; Vajont's hydraulic head was always less than its 262 m structural height due to the lower reservoir level). Rejected because the master article's primary ranking is structural height; no per-dam article in the staged 20 advertises a hydraulic-head ranking that would conflict.

This is a curator-bounded `source_defined` instance — universe is master-article-defined top-K under the man-made-only filter rule. An audit could request expansion (top-25, all-dams) or scope-rule revision based on alternative balancing of universe-coverage, semantic-schema-coherence, and source-faithfulness.
